note: Deliberate departures from the experiment brief, each recorded with what was requested, what was implemented, why, and the author's decision. The manuscript audit fails if an amendment is undecided or if the implementation no longer matches what was approved, so a deviation cannot pass merely because a gate is silent.

amendments.title: Stepsize scale and pilot design
amendments.requested: One pilot target, h = eta * h_cert, largest admissible multiplier.
amendments.implemented: One pilot per target family; h = eta / (beta_star * max(lambda_0_star_max, 1)); fastest admissible multiplier, minimised across the families; FB--GVI additionally held at the ceiling its own theorem admits.
amendments.reason: The requested rule diverges on six of the twelve final grid cells. The Fisher-Rao certificate reduces to 1/(2 kappa_star) on these targets, so its conservatism grows like kappa_star and a multiplier chosen at kappa_star = 11 is far outside the stable range at kappa_star = 2. A multiple of 1/beta_star alone fails the other way, ignoring an initial covariance that overshoots C_star by two orders of magnitude on the logistic posteriors. The scale used is the certified step with the non-attained growth allowance removed and the initialisation kept, and one pilot cell cannot calibrate both regimes.
amendments.cost: The frozen multiplier is a single number across a grid on which beta_star varies by a factor of five, so on the least conditioned cells h*gamma_star approaches 2 and the Fisher-Rao iteration count rises. That is visible in Figure 2(d) and separated from the geometry by Figure 2(e).

amendments.title: Logistic expectation rule
amendments.requested: A common quasi-Monte-Carlo update design, an independent finer evaluation design, and a still finer reference design.
amendments.implemented: Deterministic panelled Gauss-Legendre integration of the exact one-dimensional predictor marginals, order 48 for updates and order 96 for the objective evaluation and the reference solve.
amendments.reason: The logistic potential depends on theta only through the linear predictors z_i = x_i . theta, and z_i is a scalar Gaussian under q, so every expectation is a one-dimensional integral and no sampling error need be incurred. The plan's structure is preserved, since the evaluation rule is distinct from and strictly finer than the update rule and both are common to all methods; only the size of the residual disagreement changes. Against an order-160 rule the order-48 objective, gradient and Hessian differ by at most 6.6e-11, 6.5e-12 and 2.9e-11, where a 4096-point scrambled-Sobol design misplaced the objective by about 1e-1 and left a design-transfer error near 1e-3.
amendments.cost: The backend is quadrature, not a random design, so it cannot be described as quasi-Monte-Carlo and its accuracy is to the reported numerical precision rather than literally exact.

amendments.title: Reference acceptance criterion
amendments.requested: The Fisher-Rao residual at least two orders of magnitude below the smallest reported objective gap.
amendments.implemented: The residual is converted into a bound on the reference's own suboptimality by Fisher-Rao gradient domination, and that certified gap is compared with the smallest gap the panels draw.
amendments.reason: A residual is a gradient norm and a gap is an energy difference; comparing them directly compares different units. The conversion uses a proved inequality with a constant the campaign computes exactly. The Bures-Wasserstein form of the lemma is slightly tighter but was rejected: certifying a Fisher-Rao method with a Wasserstein quantity would place that geometry inside the methodology rather than leaving it an external baseline. The literal test would instead require the panels to stop at a much larger gap, since the residuals are near 1e-13 while the plotted gaps reach 1e-16.
amendments.cost: The worst reference carries 6.86 decades of margin rather than the literal residual-against-gap comparison the brief names.

amendments.title: Display name of the Bures-Wasserstein baseline
amendments.requested: FB--GVI, the name Diao et al. give the algorithm.
amendments.implemented: BW-FB in figures and manuscript text, with FB--GVI named in the figure captions so the citation is unambiguous. Stored identifiers, configs and manifests keep FB--GVI unchanged.
amendments.reason: FR-R and FR-KL name their geometry before their discretization; FB--GVI names only its discretization, which left the three labels asymmetric and the Fisher-Rao versus Bures-Wasserstein contrast unreadable from a legend. Plain BW was rejected as it names a geometry whose other algorithms this study excludes by design.
amendments.cost: It is not the published name, so the captions must carry the correspondence.

amendments.title: Three external comparators added, each with its own published safeguard
amendments.requested: A comparison restricted to FR--R, FR--KL and FB--GVI, with no method stabilised by covariance clipping.
amendments.implemented: Sq--NGVI (Kumar et al. 2025, Algorithm 1), Price--BBVI (Kim et al. 2026, SPGD with the Bonnet--Price estimator) and BBVI--STL (Kim et al. 2024, projected SGD with the STL estimator) added, each implemented as published. Price--BBVI's closed-form entropy proximal step and BBVI--STL's projection onto Lambda_S are applied because they are part of the algorithms' definitions and of the domains their guarantees are stated on; every projection activation is counted and reported. Sq--NGVI has no safeguard and its factor breakdowns are recorded as failures.
amendments.reason: Restricted to three methods the campaign can only say that Fisher--Rao differs from Bures--Wasserstein; it cannot say whether the difference is geometric. Price--BBVI shares its estimator with S--FB--GVI and its parameter space with BBVI--STL, which turns the comparison into a two-way one between geometry and estimator. Omitting a published safeguard would not be a fairer comparison, it would be a comparison against an algorithm nobody proposed.
amendments.cost: Two of the three comparators cannot produce an invalid covariance, so their failure counts are not comparable with ours. The BBVI--STL projection radius needs the target's log-smoothness in the original coordinates; that is a closed-form property of the model rather than an optimizer-whitened constant, so it does not weaken the implementable-stepsize claim, but it is one more quantity the baseline needs and ours do not.

amendments.title: An implementable stepsize rule for the practical benchmark
amendments.requested: The frozen practical multiplier of amendment A, applied to 1/(beta_star max(lambda_0_star_max, 1)).
amendments.implemented: For the real-data benchmark and the scaling study only, a dyadic grid h_0 2^{-k} whose base scale is 1 for the affine-equivariant natural-gradient updates and 1/lambda_max(H(a_0)) for the Euclidean ones, screened on stability and selected by lowest training objective after a fixed pilot budget on a disjoint subsample of the training rows. The theorem-diagnostic panels keep their certified steps and the earlier practical panels keep the amendment A multipliers. The admissibility screen acts on the whole pilot path rather than on its endpoint: a candidate is rejected if the covariance condition number ever exceeds 1e10. Calibration uses three independent problem instances where the problem is randomly generated, taking the most conservative choice, and the batch size the deployment will use.
amendments.reason: The amendment A scale is written in optimizer-whitened quantities, so computing it requires C_star. That is legitimate for a theorem diagnostic and indefensible for a benchmark: a comparison whose stepsizes were chosen with the optimizer in hand is easy to dismiss however carefully the rest was done. Three weaknesses of the first version were each found by a check rather than by inspection. An endpoint-only screen accepted a step that drove the covariance condition number to 4.7e10 within a few iterations, needing a roundoff repair; a screen on the objective's excursion was tried first and rejected, because it also rejects the KL/Bregman scheme's benign first-step transient, which raises the objective twentyfold at a conditioning that never exceeds 62 and converges 30 times faster than any admissible alternative; a single-instance pilot selected a step that diverged on the next draw of the same family; and calibrating at the benchmark batch size selected a step that diverged at the batch size the panel actually used.
amendments.cost: Each method is now tuned per problem, so the benchmark carries a tuning cost that is charged and reported rather than assumed free. Selections that land on an endpoint of the candidate grid are bounds rather than choices and are reported as censored. The conditioning screen is a property of the iterate rather than of the trajectory's shape, so a method with a large but well-conditioned transient keeps its fastest admissible step.

amendments.title: Real datasets replace synthetic ones in the headline logistic comparison
amendments.requested: Bayesian logistic regression on synthetic designs with controlled feature conditioning.
amendments.implemented: Five real binary-classification posteriors (pima, wdbc, ionosphere, sonar, spambase) fetched from OpenML, pinned by SHA-256, cached locally, standardised with training-split statistics and given an intercept. The synthetic conditioning sweep is retained in the online appendix.
amendments.reason: The synthetic cells control conditioning exactly, which makes them a good theorem diagnostic and no evidence at all that the methods work on data anyone has. A proper Gaussian prior keeps every real posterior strongly log-concave and smooth with constants in closed form, so nothing leaves the hypotheses.
amendments.cost: Conditioning is no longer a swept variable but a property of each dataset, so the appendix retains the synthetic sweep for the controlled statement. The campaign now depends on an external source, mitigated by committed digests and a local cache that makes reruns network-free.

amendments.title: The main text is compressed and an online appendix added
amendments.requested: Three main-text figures covering the deterministic mechanisms.
amendments.implemented: Four main-text figures and one accounting table: geometry and affine invariance, a compressed global-to-local figure, stochastic mechanisms, and the real-data practical benchmark. The full log-cosh grid, the synthetic logistic sweep, the elapsed-flow-time panel and the dimensional scaling move to an online appendix built from the same campaign. The stochastic figure measures the cancellation, both factors of the Delta t / B floor, and the quadratic rescue.
amendments.reason: The stochastic theory of Section 4 had no numerical demonstration at all, and the deterministic section carried corroboration the main text does not need. The paper is also long enough that adding material without removing any would work against it.
amendments.cost: Two representative log-cosh trajectories and the elapsed-flow-time comparison are no longer in the main text, so the separation of stepsize from geometry now rests on an appendix panel that the main text points to. An earlier version of the stochastic figure measured the O(1/N) tail of a decreasing-stepsize schedule. That theorem is in an earlier draft of the manuscript and not in the current one, so the panel validated a result the paper does not state. It was replaced by a stepsize sweep of the stationary floor, which measures the Delta t factor of a floor the paper does state and which no other panel checked; the decreasing-step configs were removed rather than left unplotted.
